blocks.text: The aorta is the largest and largest artery in the body. It arises from the left ventricle of the heart and extends to the abdomen, where it bifurcates into two common iliac arteries. In particular, it provides oxygenated blood to all parts of the body via systemic circulation,

blocks.text: 1-Aortic orifice of the left ventricle:

Circular fibrous ring measuring on average 25 mm in diameter formed of a fibrous ring into which 3 semi-lunar valves (sigmoid) are inserted, including a non-coronary sigmoid and two right and left coronary sigmoids.
It is attached to the other fibrous rings of the heart by the two fibrous trigones and has a close relationship with the left branch of the atrioventricular bundle of Hiss,
It projects forward from the sternal end of the left third costal cartilage to the midline opposite the fourth intercostal space.

Pathology: The aorta can be the site of several attacks. It can be dilated, we speak of an abdominal aortic aneurysm or an ascending aortic aneurysm. It can be torn in its thickness. We then speak of aortic dissection, the main cause of which is high blood pressure. There may be congenital malformations at this level, the most common being coarctation of the aorta (severe narrowing at the level of the aortic isthmus.

blocks.text: It can be affected by atheroma, wall calcium overload of the aorta. Significant chest trauma can lead to tearing of the aorta, most often at the level of the aortic isthmus (junction between a fixed aorta and a more mobile aorta).

The richness of aortic pathology, and its detailed anatomy with its different thoraco-abdominal segments encourage us to have a perfect knowledge of the anatomical bases of the largest systemic artery of the human body.

? The aorta is responsible for transporting oxygen rich blood from heart to the rest of the body. ? The aorta begins at the left ventricle of the heart, extending upward into the chest to form an arch, It then continues downward into the deep chest (descending aorta) and abdomen (abdominal aorta), where it branches into the iliac arteries just above the pelvis. ?
